# Multi-Level Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document expands the phase sequence of
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Refactoring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md) into
> **three levels of tasks that can be committed and verified independently**.
>
> RFC-039 is the sole authority for phase order and acceptance gates; this document is responsible
> only for decomposition to an executable granularity and for registering conflicts that remain
> undecided.

## Scope and Positioning

| Level       | Count       | Meaning                                                                                           |
| ----------- | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10) | Phases, in one-to-one correspondence with RFC-039's phase sequence                                |
| **Level 2** | 73          | Task groups: work groups decomposed by phase, capable of being staffed and archived independently |
| **Level 3** | 268         | Work units that can be committed and verified independently                                       |

**Reserved numbers (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`; after the LALRPOP
route was withdrawn, `8.4` / `8.5` / `8.6` were also left unassigned (2026-11-25). None of these
three numbers has ever had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established—the full history of
this document has zero hits for the three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1`
(`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md` can verify this), and there
are no repository-wide references either. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test
revival and completion): that phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`, so P8's numbering is
aligned with its phase numbers (phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth).

**Covered by this document**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding
of acceptance criteria.

**Not covered by this document**: the design rationale for individual tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the
justification for phase ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered level-two/level-three rows
**must contain two fields**—“**owning phase**” (the P phase to which the task truly belongs, which
may differ from the containing section) and “**blocks the critical path**”;
`registered, awaiting scheduling` is no longer the default state, and an unmarked task is considered
**not schedulable**. Numbers must be **unique throughout the document** (tasks on different tracks
use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and must not occupy an `N.x` number).

**Closure registration (effective 2026-11-24)**: checked rows contain only four items—the task ID,
status, **implementation commit short hash** (7 characters), and issue number (only when
applicable)—on one line:
`- [x] **3.24.1 Remaining pattern-matching completion items** ✅ 4d608df3 (issue #405)`. **Do not
write the fix, the criterion chain, gate values, file line numbers, test names, or review
conclusions**: those belong in the commit message (`git show <short-hash>`). This table is a
dashboard, not a process chronicle. **Do not write adjudication labels or restate conclusions**:
“user adjudication A/B/C,” “option A,” and “the final implementation is…” must not appear in this
table—the dashboard answers only “is it complete?” For adjudications and results, consult commit
messages and the RFC-039 decision registry.

**Short hashes are determined after the push**: a closure row records the short hash on `origin/dev`
after the push has completed. The order is **push the implementation commit first, then write the
closure row** (see “Commit hash is taken after push” in
[commit-convention](../commit-convention.md)). The closure commit itself does not carry a
hash—self-reference is impossible.

**Count columns contain only numbers**: the level-one/level-two/level-three counts under “Scope and
Positioning” contain only current values; change history such as `+1 = …` must not be included in
the table.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the “implementation points” from eight documents into this table, **five hard
gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now been resolved:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Resolution                                                                                                                                     |
| --- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 has no implementation steps whatsoever**. RFC-039 defines P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents contains a section describing how the split should be performed; `01-routing.md`'s directory tree contains one mention of `annotations.rs`, the only such reference in the entire batch                                                                                      | The P5 steps are supplied by this document (see below)                                                                                         |
| G2  | **The three ownership points for the `include!` refactor have no implementation**. RFC-039 lists it under P4; `02` assigns the cross-reference to itself; and S7 of `06` also lists it. However, `02`'s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) does **not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**                                                                                                                                                      | The implementation steps are assigned to §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); the references in RFC-039 and `06` now point here    |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts**. `RFC-039` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + one `cargo test`; `07` separately lists four checks (all with different names); and `04` previously listed `check-synth-boundary.py` (that script was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24). After deduplication, there are **at least nine new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9 | See §P9 of this document for the unified list (10 active scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents must refer to this table       |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life or death of `precedence_inline.rs`**. `06` counts it among the “1,005 lines that must be revived,” while B6 in the same document says it and the `Precedence` enum “must be deleted together”; `05` advocates deletion                                                                                                                                                                                                     | **Revive in P1, retain in P8** (decision registry C1; Pratt is no longer to be deleted)                                                        |
| G5  | **Conflicting descriptions of the L2 objective**: RFC-039 and the index of this directory once said “grammar-driven syntax”                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | This has converged on a **declarative precedence table + an unambiguous language surface** ([05](05-frontend-paradigm.md) §Syntax); see P8 8.3 |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0 仓库维护机制与代码放置规程 08 ← 新增，先立规矩
P1 复活孤儿测试并修缺陷 06 §S1
P2 建立等价性判据基线 07 全部
P3 修正确性漏洞（最小方案） 02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4 阶段契约与统一 Driver 02
P5 checker 文件内拆分 02 + 本文补齐
P6 类型表示单一化 03
P7 中间表示 SSA 化 04 } 可并行
P8 前端范式变更 05 }
P9 防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单） 01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正 06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions (do not invent; do not pad endlessly; patch when
a refactor is required) constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be established before work
begins; otherwise, while reviving tests in P1, work would already be adding `mod` declarations to
`tests/mod.rs`—precisely the cause of the G4 conflict.

### P3 Fix Correctness Defects (Minimal Solution)

Source: the defect-fix half of [02](02-stage-contract.md) §Implementation Points S3 + **the
silent-discard-point audit of 2026-10-07 (3.4)**

> **Semantic-correction routing (D59, adjudicated 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect for which “the old behavior did not constitute success”—**A silent failure / B
> silent mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, silently
> incorrect answer)—it **may be fixed alongside the refactor**, but all four requirements must be
> met: ① fail first, then pass (the failing criterion must exist beforehand and genuinely fail); ②
> do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that “previously compiled
> successfully and ran correctly” (they must not become failures, and their existing diagnostic
> codes/text/exit codes must not be changed); ③ register it in the same commit (mark the error
> category on this row + add a revision note for the phase + include the “error category” line in
> the PR's mandatory block); ④ regenerate the baseline in the same commit + manually review the
> diff. **D user-visible semantics / E external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must
> still be adjudicated first. See
> [07 §Routing criteria for semantic corrections](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded
> criteria and A–F allowlist; the “default super-refactor + post-hoc registration” approach is not
> adopted** (reason: see RFC-039 D59: without a failing criterion, fixes and regressions cannot be
> distinguished, and this conflicts with both “no C5′” and “no relaxation of any kind”).

**Acceptance**: the defect criterion turns green, and **deliberately removing the fix must make it
fail again**. **Risk**: the new E4018 on the multi-file path is a breaking change.

**3.4 acceptance**: 3.4.1 / 3.4.2 must have failing criteria before code changes (changing code
first is prohibited); 3.4.3 is a manual review; 3.4.4–3.4.8 use C2/C3 and the 9.2 gate from P9 as
the criteria. **Risk**: the new diagnostic in 3.4.1 is a behavioral change and requires synchronized
corpus-differential baseline and CHANGELOG updates.

> **Stop-the-bleeding path**: P3 does not need to wait for all of P2. The only hard prerequisites
> for 3.1/3.2 are **2.3.2 (multi-file corpus layer) + 2.4.1/2.4.3 (two failing criteria)**;
> 2.1/2.2/2.3.1/2.3.3 (the IR verifier, snapshots, single-file differential testing, and performance
> baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects (such as
> `Sorted(3)` passing silently) must not be blocked by snapshot-infrastructure construction. 3.3
> (converting panics to diagnostics) has no prerequisite and may land at any time.

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Automatic Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**; it is separate from P10 S5 “reduce the visibility of `pub` items” (narrowing
Rust's `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must entirely precede P4**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of
all four refactoring phases; reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and baseline
updates on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new SSA IR.

| 029g deletion surface                                               | File                                                                                                               | Rewritten by which phase                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `KwPub` and grammar branches                                        | `lexer/{tokens,state,mod}.rs`; `parser/parser_state.rs`, `statements/{declarations,imports,functions,bindings}.rs` | **P8** (8.2 lexer convergence / 8.3 Pratt precedence convergence / 8.7 split `parse_assign_after_target`)                                                                                                                                                                  |
| AST `is_pub` ×2 (`Assign` / `TypeDefinition`)                       | `parser/ast.rs`                                                                                                    | **P6 6.5 dead AST variants** + P8 + D1 directory rename (`parser/ast.rs` → top-level `src/ast/`)                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `auto_bind_to_type` and the `pub` branch of `collect_exports`       | `typecheck/checker.rs`, `environment.rs`                                                                           | **P5** (`include!`→real `mod` and checker splitting are **pure moves**, and the `pub` branch will be moved unchanged into the new file)                                                                                                                                    |
| Dead-code exemptions `exempt_pub` / `is_exported` and role dispatch | `typecheck/passes/dead_code.rs`, `module/orchestrator.rs` (inside `check_project`)                                 | **P4 4.2.2** (slim down `check_project`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| The `Public` modifier of `semantic_tokens`                          | `typecheck/checker/semantic_tokens.rs`                                                                             | **P4 4.2.6** + P5 + 4.6 (D55)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `ir_gen`'s ignored `is_pub` binding                                 | `middle/core/ir_gen.rs`                                                                                            | **P7** (`ir_gen.rs` SSA conversion)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |

|                             | 029g.6.2 Diagnostic text                                                                                                     | 4 W1xxx help messages                                                                                                | They no longer claim that “pub is an external interface”; aligned with the Bin-role behavior of `dead_code.rs`                                                                                            |
| 029g.7 Documentation        | 029g.7.1 Language reference and guides                                                                                       | `reference/language-spec/{modules,syntax,language-overview}.md`, `warning-code/warning-codes.md`, `guide/modules.md` | The specification no longer contains statements contradicting the implementation, such as “pub can still be written”; the “pub never triggers W1001” statement in `warning-codes.md` is corrected as well |

**Acceptance (behavioral changes; failing criteria first)**:

1. **Fail first, then pass**: each of the two behavioral changes must first establish a failing
   criterion before code changes—① `pub` changes from “silently accepted” to a parse error; ②
   unreferenced top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items
   were absolutely exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` test case in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, they must be replaced with
   equivalent new test cases.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: the diagnostic-set changes (the new parse error + new W1001) ⇒
   update the corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in
   the same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff requires an
   explanation.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` are all green.

**Ordering**: it overlaps with the files in 3.4 (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be
serial and cannot run in parallel; **the entire track must precede P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g
track does not depend on 3.4; implementers may choose which to do first based on the context at
hand.

> **Commit comparison (2026-10-08)**: the incorporation of this section (P3.5 chapter +
> main-chain/constraint row) and RFC-039's D56 were included together in `97071c81b` during a
> parallel-flow workspace cleanup—the commit message records “3.4 supplementary registration +
> D57/D58 adjudication filing” and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; as with
> the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 implementation note), it is recorded
> in place as evidence for retrospective bisection.

|                                                  | 4.9.9 A cross-unit single-definition method called with **named arguments** loses its formal-parameter name table (registered 2026-11-25, discovered during the 7c closure round): calling a cross-unit method (injected through the registry) with named arguments reports `E1014 Function '…' has no parameter named '…' (available: )`—the name table is empty; positional calls to the same method work normally, and named-argument calls within a single file work normally. Minimal reproduction: `lib.yx` defines `Point.scale_by: (self: &Point, k: Float) -> Float`, while `main.yx` has `p.scale_by(k = 2.0)` ⇒ E1014, and `p.scale_by(2.0)` ⇒ 6.0. **D59 category: C** (old behavior was not success: named arguments were silently discarded, followed by runtime failure or a silently incorrect value). **Scope (final form after two narrowing rounds on 2026-11-26—only three additions; everything else is deletion and registration)**: ① `AstToIrGenerator::method_param_info` (`src/middle/lower/query.rs`)—use the definition unit's qualified name `{module}.{Type}.{method}[#N]` to retrieve the declaration-time formal names from the sole cross-unit carrier `ModuleInfo::method_overloads` (the candidate ↔ mixed-in IR name ↔ formal name vectors are in the same order, using the same data as the typecheck injection surface); the call site (`src/middle/lower/expr/call.rs`) uses the qualified name from `method_dispatch_name` to look up the name table, rather than two separate bare names. These two locations fix only **bare-name imports** (`local == target`) for cross-unit methods: the candidate injection surface retains the narrowed rule from before 4.9.9 (`local != target` is skipped), so named arguments for alias imports are outside the fix scope (see “Known Gaps”). ② `ModuleRegistry::all_method_bindings` (`src/frontend/module/registry.rs`) merges in **ascending module-key order**—**category C (independent of the original bug): eliminate the “same input, multiple results” behavior caused by HashMap iteration order**; this is not a fix for the original bug; the criterion = same-file unit test `test_all_method_bindings_merge_is_deterministic_across_hash_seeds` (32 registry instances with alternating insertion orders; only one single binding is allowed for the same method key; removing the ascending merge produces two results). **Criterion (fail first, then pass)**: two driver-level tests in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` (bare import with a single candidate 6.0 / two candidates selected by name as 6.0 and 30, both with value assertions; the file header contains the medical-history gate); unit tests in `src/middle/lower/tests/query.rs` (`method_param_info` empty-name-table guard ⇒ None, positive control returns a non-empty table unchanged); unit test in `src/frontend/module/registry.rs` (the deterministic criterion above). Project fixture `tests/yaoxiang-multifile/named-args-cross-unit-method` (the `alias-overload` fixture is deleted together with retirement of the alias surface); the corpus-differential baseline `tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl` now has 404 lines: **relative to the direct parent commit `ac810e97`, 405→404** (the intermediate state once contained `alias-overload`); **relative to the pre-4.9.9 baseline `08ccacc5`, 403→404** (+1 base fixture `named-args-cross-unit-method`; `alias-overload` never entered the final history). The line-count change is the inevitable result of fixtures entering and leaving (the regenerated `corpus_probe` output matches the checked-in baseline byte for byte), and is **not lost coverage**. **Known gaps (each named individually; old behavior = silently ignored or silently discarded; D60② “should report but does not,” category A)**: closure-value binding / block-body function declaration / named nested function declaration / built-in container construction other than `len` with named arguments / whole-module import / RFC-004 binding arm. **Two of these are corrected according to P0's measured semantics**: ① the **static-function form** (both local and cross-unit, definition and binding forms) is **entirely unavailable today**—local `check` reports E3006, cross-unit definition-form `run` reports E6007, and cross-unit binding-form `run` reports E6006; the positional and named arguments have the same code and are unrelated to named-argument discarding; ② **RFC-004 cross-unit positional arguments also fail** (`check` passes, `run` reports E6006), because the dispatch name is absent from the merged function table; this is also unrelated to named arguments. **Already fixed (4.9.10-S2b, D59 category A fixed in passing: old behavior E6007/E1014 was not success, so no previously successful program becomes a failure)**: ① **alias-import named arguments** (`use a.{Temp as X}` + `t.bump(k = 2.0)`); ② **namespace arms** (named arguments after `lib.Temp(..)`); ③ **inferred-receiver named arguments** (the receiver type is inferred and has no written annotation). Previously, these respectively produced runtime E6007 with silently discarded arguments and check-time E1014 (`available: `) false rejections; now all bind by declaration-time formal name (value assertion 6.0; criterion `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs`, with the red state recorded in that file's header medical-history gate). Two residual identity-surface issues remain, one of which has been closed: this unit's own same-named type + alias import (two same-named defining-side identities coexist, and the import surface cannot register the unit's own declaration) **has been closed through the import-surface closure in 4.9.10-S2a** (project fixture `same-name-type-local-and-alias-import` is fully green); the remaining issue is function-body-level/cross-scope imports being merged globally by unit (a shared import table)—this form itself does not work (an existing defect: check passes, run reports E6006), was not introduced by this batch, and was not fixed. **Deletions in this round (relative to the first six rounds of 4.9.9)**: candidate-provider precedence, candidate-signature comparison, owner/compatibility inference, the `frontend::module::import_face` shared-provider table, the IR-side “no name table ⇒ E1014” fallback, and the **E5006 ambiguity prohibition at import-name resolution**—the latter rejects mixed/alias-only forms that previously ran on the parent commit (category D), and the 2026-11-26 decision withdrew it; this round introduces no new ambiguity determination. **Visible changes**: ① cross-unit method named arguments (**bare-name imports**, including two-candidate overloads) change from an E1014 empty table to binding by name (measured 6.0 / 30); ② the remaining forms return to their pre-4.9.9 behavior (named arguments are silently ignored or discarded; see “Known Gaps”); ③ a method's single binding no longer varies with HashMap iteration order for the same input (category C). **Status**: completed 2026-11-26 (including the narrowing round and review pass). | 4.9.7         | See the criteria in `src/driver/tests/named_args_cross_unit_method.rs` and `src/driver/tests/named_args_import_shapes.rs` (the latter added with 4.9.10-S2b), and `src/frontend/module/registry.rs`; |                                                  | 4.9.10 Cross-unit method identity is undefined (registered 2026-11-25, confirmed as a structural issue during 4.9.9 implementation): the method-candidate key `{Type}.{method}` does not include module qualification, so for same-named types across modules, three consumers—candidate injection (`driver::arms::visible_method_overloads`), typecheck's formal-name/candidate matching, and IR dispatch (`method_dispatch_name`)—each guess the provider by name, and changing any one of them moves the “silent incorrect value” to another location. **Root solution**: elevate type identity to a **module-qualified identity** (`{module}.{Type}`), and change the method-candidate key accordingly to `{module}.{Type}.{method}`; one resolver produces it, and the three consumers only read it. This requires changing the shape of the `overload_resolutions` key and the mixed-in name, and is D59 **category D** (requires adjudication). **Disposition in this round (after two narrowing rounds of 4.9.9)**: 4.9.9 **introduces no new rejections**—the category-D rejection list from the first six rounds (all named arguments ⇒ E1014 / conflicting positional-argument forms ⇒ E1107 / E5006 ambiguity working order. **Residual surface (after this round closes)**: ① function-body-level/cross-scope imports are merged globally by unit (a shared import table), and this form itself does not work (an |                             | 5.1.2 Add `use super::*` or item-by-item imports (the `include!` era inherited the scope implicitly)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | 5.1.1        | `cargo build` is green                                                                                                                             |
| 5.2 Extract `refinement`    | 5.2.1 Move out the refinement blocks (three noncontiguous regions in the original `checker.rs`; now a single `checker/refinement.rs` file containing `ReturnRefinement` / `RefinedWalkCtx`), and leave the shared surface and the six cross-boundary shared items unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 5.1.1        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                       |
|                             | 5.2.2 Consolidate the refinement entry point into “`&self` + return diagnostics,” **without leaving the `impl`**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer writes to the error channel implicitly through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned upward and written at the sole call site `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Rationale for remaining in the `impl`**: the only field used by this family is `self.env` (so detaching the `impl` is technically feasible), but turning “the entry point and the entire walk into free functions” would also move these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test, and it would create a reverse dependency from the “retained surface (signature collection)” to refinement—contrary to the coupling-reduction intent of this step | 5.2.1        | —                                                                                                                                                  |
| 5.3 Extract `annotations`   | 5.3.1 Move out the 10-item annotation-validation family (now a single `checker/annotations.rs` file; `check_annotation_type_names` is the `pub(super)` entry point, the other 9 items are private to the family, and `is_predicate_head` is a free function within the family)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | 5.2.2        | C1 zero-diff                                                                                                                                       |
|                             | 5.3.2 **`collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) remains `pub(crate)` and stays under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed by both `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 **did not migrate it** as measured ⇒ the “zero call-site changes” criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Retained constraint**: if it is ever moved with the family (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add a `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | 5.3.1        | **Zero call-site changes** is the hard acceptance criterion for this step: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is ever moved with the annotation family, `checker.rs` **must then** add a
`pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export so that the import remains unchanged; 5.3 did not migrate
it as measured, so this batch did not add a re-export (the criterion was already satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—that increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields zero decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are to be split when the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

**6.9 Model and Invariants (First-Principles Rewrite, 2026-11-13)**

> **Model**: D62's end state is a **unified item world**—type positions and value positions share
> one set of compile-time items. A strength declaration produces one quantifier reading
> `q ∈ {0,1,ω}`; `q` is the **sole input** to slot allocation, and the call-site argument view and
> implementation-head binding view are two projections of the same fact. Equality is a **pure
> decision** (both sides normalize to the same thing; it does not bind type variables); evidence is
> the **sole entry point** for q=0 slots (four sources: literals/value environment/single-value
> pinning/Γ equality); erasure is the **runtime consequence** of q=0 (it holds for both closed and
> open/recursive terms); Σ constructor sites **reuse** the same evidence interface rather than
> introducing another one. **The completion criterion = the invariants hold, not that the subphase
> names have run.**

> D implementation}; C.1 is independent and complete; F4 adjudication → A.C3; decision-point
> protocol → B.d; design review → D implementation. A.C3 and B.d may run in parallel but require
> file-surface coordination (C3 leans typecheck→mono, while d leans types/solver→sema); C.2 may run

> may depend on the typed exit in 6.9.3. **P7 gate = the exits of A/B/C; D does not block.**

> **A.C3 prerequisites: F4 adjudication (option A adjudicated, 2026-11-16; measurement)**: the old
> wording “`CheckOnly` evidence does not enter the request” is obsolete—`ConstEvidence`/`CheckOnly`
> have been deleted; the current mechanism is that an open term's `normalize` returns `Unproven` ⇒
> no request is created, and the representation layer's `GenericArg::Const(ConstExpr)` can already
> hold `k-1`. **The adjudication was changed to two orthogonal decisions plus one terminal
> subdecision**: D-a representation (A: open terms enter `deferred` and are normalized before
> enqueueing / B: no specialization); D-b evaluation point (only mono is possible; C-1, reconstruct
> the second field from IR, breaks the single representation/evaluator; C-3 = A); **F4-T
> termination** (naive firing drives the recursive chain into `max_depth` and hits E3005; T-a:
> condition firing within the instance / T-b: bounded firing + fallback to the original at the
> boundary / T-c: a termination layer or change the specification). **Measure first, then
> adjudicate; before measurement, do not treat “option A is implementable” as a conclusion.** **User
> (2026-11-16): D-a=A-closed, D-b=C-3, F4-T=T-b, bound=8; C3 implementation is a separate task; do
> not claim the complete form of I4.**

> **B.d prerequisite: decision-point protocol (not yet documented)**: RFC-027 §12.1 requires
> “decision points to use unification first; after unified failure, equality may be used, but all
> partial bindings produced by the unification attempt must first be rolled back.” The
> implementation must answer: is the entry point an outer wrapper around `solver.unify` or a new
> `decide` layer; may defeq attempt only when both sides are ground (no unbound variables); what are
> the snapshot/restore boundary and cost; and do unify and defeq share one budget or each have one.
> **Responsibility boundary**: unify remains responsible for subtype/Any/Never; defeq only decides
> equivalence and does not take over subtyping; bidirectional subtyping must not be treated as
> equivalence (RFC-027 §12.1). **Provide the protocol and production call graph before writing
> code**; 6.9.3c's wiring contract wasted two rounds because it assumed `can_assign` was the
> decision point, while `AssignmentChecker` has zero production instantiations.

> **E acceptance and residuals (I8, cross-cutting)**: every slice must provide ① zero
> corpus/IR-snapshot drift or an itemized classification; ② `testsuite run fast` + affected
> integration tests; ③ error-code generator idempotence (if an emission point/code table is
> changed); ④ behavioral changes classified per D59 and implemented fail-first/pass-first. **Wiring
> tasks additionally require**: production call-graph evidence (which production entry point, how
> many paths, which path is reachable); using unit-test reachability as a substitute for user
> reachability is forbidden; rollback and budget must have measured figures. **Residual
> disposition**: #537 (category D, silent discard of proof-function formal refinement; not fixed
> before adjudication, and 6.9.4/6.9.5 must not depend on its fix), #539 (import-surface q=0;
> category-C boundary, and if it remains open, 6.9.4 covers only the module), #540 (deep-nesting
> stack overflow; **closed**—3.20.30 closed on 2026-11-14: orchestration-layer 64MB large-stack
> thread + parser depth gate MAX_PARSE_DEPTH=1024 + E0019, as recorded in 09's 3.20.30 row), #541
> (TailCall; **closed**—three sites entered and exited together on 2026-11-16:
> `call_form_is_rewritten` / `replace_calls_in_function` / `drop_erased_call_args` through the
> single rewrite point `rewritten_call_target`, covering `Call`/`TailCall`; the init section and
> function body share one site-rewriting implementation; red→green + three mutations), #542
> (orphaned shared layer; **landed (2026-11-19)**: DCE pass + post-mono two entry-point wiring +
> removal of the C2c temporary workaround; red→green, 402/402, function-table attribution and
> deviations), #552 (importing multi-parameter predicates for proof execution; adjacent to 6.9.5,

> decide whether they remain in 6.9.4's outOfScope or move to 6.9.1/the E4018 proof-function
> surface.

> **Non-claims/boundaries**: this item covers only record Σ (B: witness field), does not touch

> does not fulfill the open-constraint `Eq(N,n)` tripwire; the second value position of `f(y)(y)` is

> cover only forms that do not depend on proof-function formal refinement; if #539 is not fixed,
> 6.9.4 covers only the module; #540 is closed (3.20.30); #542 landed (2026-11-19); 2.1.4's
> inner-isolation failure was cleared on 2026-11-20 (criterion rewritten by slot identity in the

**Hard acceptance** (**revised on 2026-10-27, following the 2026-10-26 decision ②**):
`git diff --stat tests/yaoxiang tests/baselines src/std/` must be **empty in every round of
6.1–6.7**. **Direct-driver test files** under `tests/` (tests that directly drive changed code, such
as `tests/formatter_integration.rs`) may be modified when mechanically required by the change, but
each modification must be registered with **file / line count / reason**; **tests must not be
deleted, and assertions must not be weakened**. **Exception**: 6.8.2 is a **behavioral-fix** batch
(new diagnostic code + baseline update), does not fall under this hard acceptance criterion, and is
handled as a separate round with separate adjudication.

> **Revision relationship**: the original wording of 2026-10-26 (decision ②) was
> `git diff --stat tests/ src/std/`, applying a blanket zero-difference requirement to the entire
> `tests/` directory; the revised wording **changes only direct-driver test files from “zero
> difference” to “may be changed but must register file / line count / reason”**, while the
> zero-difference requirement for the **corpus layer (`tests/yaoxiang`), baseline layer
> (`tests/baselines`), and standard library (`src/std/`)** remains unchanged. First application =
> 6.1.2: only `tests/formatter_integration.rs` changed by **3 lines** (2 occurrences of
> `assert_format_eq` changed from `i64`→`Int64` + 1 comment line), with the reason = the expected
> type-name spelling changed by the modified spelling requirement, so the assertion had to be
> synchronized; no tests were deleted and no assertions weakened. See “P6 6.1 Name Canonicalization
> Closure.”

**Risk**: the precedence table is the sole authority, and missing a consumer will **silently change
associativity** (no error, only a changed parse result). The defenses are the permanent D1–D3
assertions and operator-property cross-validation tests; every new operator must enter both the
table and the cross-validation tests.

> **8.3–8.6 depend on D0/D2 from `08`**: if the grammar file is placed outside `parser/`, or action
> code references `sema` in reverse, it will be blocked by `check-boundary.py`.

## Implementation Points: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stop-the-bleeding path (adjudicated 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to
> **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 + 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two failing criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR
> verifier, 2.2 snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential testing and performance baseline) may proceed in
> parallel with P3. Stopping the bleeding from correctness defects must not be blocked by
> criterion-infrastructure construction; however, **P4 must still wait for all of P2**—the unified
> Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every action in P1 (1.2.x is precisely the act of adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Defect criteria must **be written in a failing state first** (2.4.1/2.4.3), and the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the failing tests have somewhere to run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order would cause bugs to become codified as “existing behavior” by the phase table                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers the rewrite targets of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (the list is in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` refactor and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated; otherwise, regressions cannot be located by bisection                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations do not converge first, the new IR will grow into a third representation; **P7 gate = the exits of phases A/B/C in 6.9** (I1–I3, I5, I7; namely 6.9.2 including C3, 6.9.3 including d, and completed 6.9.4); D (Σ) does not block; P7 may consume only quantifier-derived views and the defeq interface and must not create a parallel ledger; the 7.0 pure-move batch is a P7 prerequisite and is not subject to this gate, but it must not consume the undecided defeq/quantifier interfaces |
| P7/P8 → P9                | 9.5's snapshot baseline and 9.3's `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                      | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC-039)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                             |
| B                                          | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`; revert file by file                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| C                                          | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three layers of criteria are mutually independent                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| D                                          | 4.4 (proof-layer completion) ∥ the entire P6 track                                 | `02` explicitly states in S5 that it “should proceed independently of S1–S4”                                                                                                                                                                              |
| E                                          | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All become independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| F                                          | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | 9.5's snapshot baseline must be captured last                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| G                                          | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified 2026-10-05: S3 modifies `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 modifies `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 modifies two `pub` locations in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (the B6/E5
same-batch files); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` / `environment.rs`
are the same files—the external track's delete-pub batch and the silent-channel fix must be serial).

**Additional internal-document constraints**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial; 7.0 →
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial (7.0 is the P7 pure-move batch), and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is established as an independent phase rather than merged into P9**—gates are “post-hoc
  checks,” while rules are “prior judgment.” P9's scripts cannot prevent “patching when a refactor
  is required”; only D0–D4's review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the three coexisting lists that caused
  original gap G3 prevented closure. This table merges them: ten active scripts, each owned by one
  phase (9.8 was cancelled by the user on 2026-11-24), with report-only status and conversion timing
  explicitly traceable.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an “independent track to be done after the
  refactor”**—its deletion surface overlaps with the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039
  D56). Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar,
  new checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and
  RFC status correction into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplied by this document rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding checker splitting would exceed the granularity at which changes can
  be rolled back.
- **5.3.2 uses “zero call-site changes” as hard acceptance**—the split must be independently
  revertible.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criteria**—it only says that “the fixed defects
  must not be rolled back,” and lacks a requirement to record “what was fixed.” **Execution
  convention**: the commit message for every 1.3.x fix must cite the fixed test name and defect
  description as evidence for retrospective bisection.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b, two
  exclusive commits, per DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 renamed references; missing one **silently
  changes associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding level-three tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 landed as
  7e.1, D20 landed as 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was incorporated into 7e.1, while
  deletion remains in P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally intended as an “independent issue”**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: `2341` was incorporated into 7e.3; `2315` was rechecked on 2026-11-28 and
  found to be an audit false positive (the field has no producer, and the language layer has no
  throw/try/catch), so 7e.2 was cancelled and the exception remnants were assigned to P10 S6.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**:
  incorporated into P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode gate extractor) has ambiguous ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into the generation-time gate task in P10 S6.
